messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposal: blended retainer + consumption SLA (pricing scenarios)

Hi Maya + Elliot —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised I'm sending a concise proposal with two paths we think will match Brightline's reliability needs while keeping unit economics predictable as your token volumes ramp. The attached PDF (Redwood-SLA-Hybrid-Proposal-v1.pdf) has full tables; quick summary below: 

- Option A: Baseline retainer + low overage credits
  - Monthly retainer: $18,000 (covers 24/7 on-call and guaranteed warm standby for one zone)
  - Included escalation hours: 40 H/mo (triage + remediation)
  - Overage: $150/hr beyond included hours
  - Uptime SLA: 99.95% across primary region; multi-region failover available as add-on

- Option B: Consumption-forward (smaller retainer, higher credits)
  - Monthly retainer: $6,000 (business-hours on-call, priority queue)
  - Included escalation hours: 8 H/mo
  - Credits per 100k tokens above commit: $45/100k tokens (volume pricing tiers in PDF)
  - Uptime SLA: 99.9% with optional 99.95% uplift for committed spend

Recommendation: a blended approach — start with Option B + a 3-month pilot where Brightline pre-commits to a modest monthly token volume. After pilot, convert to Option A if you require full 24/7 guaranteed warm standby. This reduces short-term cost while giving you a path to a hardened SLA.

Questions for you to unblock procurement:
- Which SLA band do you need contractually at go-live (99.9% vs 99.95%)?
- Is Brightline open to a 3-month pilot commit (we can structure pro-rated credits)?
- Any specific on-call routing requirements (PagerDuty/Snowflake/Teams integrations)?

Next steps: if you confirm the target SLA and pilot commit by Aug 12, we can send a redlineable SOW + pricing sheet and lock these rates for 60 days.

Cheers,
Alex

Thanks Alex — helpful breakdown. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Our initial production window will be global (US + EU primary), so multi-region failover is required in the contract. Can you confirm whether the 99.95% SLA in Option A covers both regions, or whether it's per-region?

2) For on-call: we need true 24/7 escalation for Sev 1 incidents and an SLA-backed response time (30 minutes acknowledgement). Is that baked into the retainer or an add-on?

3) Regarding pricing, we typically need a 12-month price lock for budgeting. Are the rates above lockable at signature if we take the pilot?

Would like to see an example monthly billing cadence showing retainer, included hours, and a sample overage calculation for a month with a 25% spike. If possible, can you add a short clause around credits for sustained outages (event credits) in the SOW?

–Maya
Maya Patel

Hi Maya — great questions, answered inline below. I'll also attach a redlineable SOW draft if this direction looks good.

1) Multi-region SLA: Option A's 99.95% uptime is measurable per-region. For a contract that treats the service as "global" we can provide a blended SLA (combined availability) at 99.95% for the service across both regions, but that requires a 12-month committed capacity and a 15% uplift on the retainer to cover cross-region warm standby. I'll note both figures in the SOW (retainer + 15% uplift option).

2) 24/7 escalation and acknowledgement: included in Option A (the retainer covers 24/7 triage, with a contractual acknowledgement time of 30 minutes for Sev 1). Option B requires an add-on to reach the same acknowledgement SLA (we've priced that at $6,500/mo as a "Sev1 30-min guarantee"). All on-call rotations are routed through your PagerDuty instance; we support PagerDuty and Opsgenie out of the box.

3) 12-month price lock: yes — if Brightline signs the SOW and a Master Services Agreement (MSA) that references the pricing table, we will lock the rates for 12 months (pilot period excluded if pilot is < 3 months; we propose pilot counts toward the 12 months only if you commit up front).

Billing cadence example (illustrative month):
- Base retainer (Option A): $18,000
- Included escalation hours consumed: 30/40
- Overage hours (10 @ $150) = $1,500
- Incident credit for a sustained outage (example): if more than 2 hours of total regional downtime attributable to Redwood, we offer a pro-rated credit equal to 5% of that month’s retainer (SOW will formalize thresholds)
- Month total: $19,500 (before tax)

I'll attach a quick one-page sample invoice and SOW draft. If you want the multi-region 99.95% as a global guarantee, we'll show both standard and uplifted numbers so procurement can see the delta.

I'll put a small concession in the SOW: 7.5% introductory discount on the retainer for the first 3 months if you sign within 14 days.

Thanks — planning to follow up with a SOW and a sample invoice by EOD.

Best,
Alex

Hi Maya — quick note from procurement/legal side: 

- We can commit to a 12-month price lock at signature; as Alex said, pilot months will count toward the locked term only if Brightline pays the pilot commitment upfront.
- For multi-region coverage, we typically create a single SOW with a region appendix that spells out per-region measurement and blended credit logic. That appendix also defines the pass/fail criteria for outage credits so there's no ambiguity.
- Regarding credits: we prefer explicit credit slabs (example: 0.5–1.0 hours = 2% credit, 1–3 hours = 5% credit, >3 hours = 12% credit of monthly retainer). We'll propose those slabs in the SOW and include an on-call runbook addendum.

Procurement ask: if you can provide a rough projected monthly token usage for months 1–6 (the Brightline-Usage-Profile.xlsx you sent helps), we'll produce a tiered discount schedule tied to a 6/12/18 month commit. Typical discounts: 5% @ 6m, 10% @ 12m, 15% @ 18m commit (applied to per-token unit price only).

If you confirm the commit tier by COB Aug 14, we can include the appropriate discount row in the SOW.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Alex/Laura — thanks for the breakdown. Internal notes: Brightline's finance + legal prefer the blended approach; we want to avoid a heavy upfront retainer but need the 24/7 Sev1 guarantee. Our suggested path: 

1) Sign a 6-month pilot with Option B (smaller retainer $6k) + add the Sev1 30-min guarantee add-on ($6.5k) so we get the acknowledgement SLA immediately.
2) Embed a 12-month price lock in the MSA to start at pilot signature date.
3) At month-3 review: if uptime and incident economics are within agreed thresholds, convert to Option A with the 15% cross-region uplift for 99.95% global (effective month-4).

Can you send the redlineable SOW + MSA with the discount rows and outage credit slabs? We can get procurement review on Monday. Also, please include a DocuSign link and a sample invoice format. If those are in the packet we can target an Aug 21 signature.

Appreciate the 7.5% introductory concession — that helps.
